name: EPCQ16ASI8N
title: EPCQ-A serial configuration flash: 4, 16, 32, 64 and 128 Mbit, AS x1 and AS x4, 2.7 V to 3.6 V
summary: The EPCQ-A family are non-volatile serial flash memories that hold an FPGA's configuration image and feed it to the FPGA over the active serial interface, one bit wide (AS x1) or four bits wide (AS x4). Five densities run from 4 Mbit to 128 Mbit; the three smaller ones come in an 8-pin SOIC and the two larger in a 16-pin SOIC. They run from 2.7 V to 3.6 V over -40 °C to 85 °C, clock at up to 100 MHz (50 MHz for the plain read), endure over 100,000 program-erase cycles and retain data for over 20 years. EPCQ16ASI8N is the 16 Mbit part in the 8-pin SOIC.

operation.text: The device stores an FPGA configuration image and supplies it over the active serial interface, in AS x1 or AS x4 (EPCQ4A: AS x1 only). It can also be reprogrammed in-system from an external microprocessor with the SRunner driver, or through an Intel FPGA Download Cable II, Download Cable or Ethernet Cable. By default the array is erased, with every bit at 1. SFDP (JEDEC) is supported.

An operation starts with nCS falling. The 8-bit operation code goes in on DATA0, then any address or data bytes, each bit latched on a DCLK rising edge; all bytes travel MSB first. Read data comes out on DATA[3:0] and nCS may be raised at any bit of it. For a write or erase, nCS has to rise on a byte boundary (a whole multiple of 8 clocks) or the operation is discarded. While a write or erase cycle runs, every attempt to reach the array is refused and the cycle carries on.

Opcode and a 24-bit address A[23..0] go in on DATA0; data then shifts out on DATA1 on falling DCLK edges, at up to 50 MHz. The address counts up after each byte and wraps from the top address to 000000h, so one command can read the whole array and keeps going until nCS rises. Raw Programming Data (.rpd) bytes come out LSB first. Ignored, without disturbing it, if issued during a write or erase cycle.

Like read bytes but followed by 8 dummy clocks after the address, and clocked at up to 100 MHz. The address auto-increments and wraps to 000000h; nCS high at any point in the output ends it. Ignored during an erase, program or write cycle.

operation.topic: Extended dual and quad fast reads (BBh, EBh)
operation.text: BBh carries address and data two bits per clock on DATA0 and DATA1, with 4 dummy clocks; EBh carries them four bits per clock on DATA0 to DATA3, with 6 dummy clocks. The pins turn from input to output after the dummy clocks. EBh is not available on EPCQ4A.

9Fh is followed by two dummy bytes and returns the 8-bit device ID on DATA1. ABh (EPCQ4A, EPCQ16A and EPCQ64A only) is followed by three dummy bytes and returns the 8-bit silicon ID on DATA1, repeating it for as long as DCLK runs with nCS low. Both are ignored during a write or erase cycle.

06h sets the write enable latch (WEL). Write bytes (02h), quad input fast write bytes (32h), write status (01h), erase bulk (C7h), erase sector (D8h) and erase subsector (20h) each need it set first. 04h clears it. WEL also returns to 0 on its own at power-up and when a write bytes, quad input fast write bytes, write status, erase bulk or erase sector operation completes.

operation.topic: Write bytes (02h) and quad fast write (32h)
operation.text: After write enable, send the opcode, a 24-bit address and 1 to 256 data bytes, holding nCS low throughout. Bytes that run past the end of the 256-byte page wrap to the start of the same page. Over 256 bytes, only the last 256 are kept; under 256, only the addressed bytes change. The self-timed program cycle (tWB) starts when nCS rises; WIP reads 1 until it ends. Bytes are to be erased before they are written. 32h is the same with data entering four bits per clock on DATA0 to DATA3 (not EPCQ4A).

Erasing sets bits to 1 (FFh) and needs write enable first. C7h erases the whole array and takes no address; it runs only when all block protect bits are 0. D8h erases the 64 KB sector holding the given 24-bit address, 20h the 4 KB subsector. Each starts a self-timed cycle (tEB, tES, tESS) when nCS rises; WIP is 1 until it ends, and WEL is cleared before the end.

05h reads the status register, repeatedly while clocks continue, at any time including during a write or erase. 01h, after write enable, writes TB and BP[2:0] (WEL and WIP are untouched); sectors covered by the block protect setting then behave as read-only. The self-timed write status cycle takes 10 ms typical, 15 ms at most (tWS); WIP is 1 during it.

Reads the 256-byte Serial Flash Discoverable Parameter table (JESD216A), which describes the device's configuration and operations. The 24-bit address has A[23..8] = 0 and A[7..0] as the starting byte; after 8 dummy clocks the data comes out MSB first from the falling edge of the 40th DCLK. Not available on EPCQ4A.

With nCS low the device is in active mode (ICC1); configuration of the FPGA happens in this mode. After nCS goes high it stays active until any internal write or erase cycle has finished, then drops to standby (ICC0).
On EPCQ64A and EPCQ128A, nRESET held low for about 1 µs aborts any operation and returns the device to its power-on state. It has an internal pull-up (RPR, 300 kΩ to 1000 kΩ).

Intel Quartus Prime generates a Programmer Object File (.pof) for the chosen EPCQ-A density. The SRunner driver reads .rpd files and programs the device from an embedded processor in about the time Quartus takes. The FPGA reads .rpd data LSB first, so .rpd bytes are shifted out LSB first on reads and shifted in LSB first on writes. In ISP with a download cable, the cable drives the FPGA's nCONFIG low, overrides the 10 kΩ pull-down on the FPGA's nCE pin, programs the device over the AS pins, then releases them and pulses nCONFIG to start configuration. The FPGA can also program it over JTAG with the Serial Flash Loader (SFL).
